claims.text: An ultra-nanocrystalline, dynamically amorphized surface layer promotes oxidation resistance in MPEAs exposed to harsh high-temperature oxidizing environments.
The surface layer preserves material integrity by acting as a diffusion barrier that retards oxygen ingress.
The surface layer supports formation of a self-healing oxide.
CoCrFeMnNi provides an example of a single-phase, initially coarse-grained MPEA.
Controlled deformation or rapid thermal cycling can induce dynamic amorphization and generate an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer.
The proposed governing behavior applies during sustained oxidation in air at approximately 600–900 °C.
Dynamic amorphization produces an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer characterized by high-angle grain boundaries.
A high density of grain boundaries in the surface layer acts as an effective barrier to oxygen diffusion.
The surface grain boundaries encourage formation of a mixed metal-oxide scale.
The mixed metal-oxide scale is self-healing.
The processed alloy will have a significantly lower oxidation rate than an untreated coarse-grained baseline.
The processed alloy will exhibit less oxide-scale spallation than the baseline.
The processed alloy will retain mechanical properties better than the baseline, including reduced brittleness or creep during thermal cycling.
The hypothesis should hold for compositionally similar MPEAs between approximately 600 and 900 °C in oxidizing environments.
The hypothesis may not apply to alloys that cannot undergo dynamic amorphization or that possess substantially different phase structures.

contradictions.description: The layer is described as dynamically amorphized or an 'amorphized nanolayer' while also being described as ultra-nanocrystalline and governed by a high density of grain boundaries. A fully amorphous layer lacks crystalline grains and grain boundaries, so the intended final structure is internally ambiguous.
